source: PLACEHOLDER, synthetic. Ballpark lodging values informed by EIA CBECS lodging end-use shares and ENERGY STAR hotel benchmarks (site EUI roughly 80 to 100 kBtu/ft2 in cold climates). Setpoint sensitivities (about 3% heating and 4% cooling energy per degree F) and driver weights are rules of thumb to be replaced or confirmed (docs/11 Phase 7). Recovery after a setback is an illustrative placeholder: 0.15 kBtu per room per degree F is roughly the air in a 3,000 ft3 room (about 0.05) plus some furnishings, 2 returns per booked room per day, and equipment efficiency of 0.8 (gas) or 2.3 (heat pump) for heating and COP 3 for cooling; if research shows the per-degree sensitivities are already net of recovery, set kBtuPerRoomPerF to 0.

finance.source: Price growth: EIA Annual Energy Outlook 2026 (April 2026), Counterfactual Baseline case, nominal commercial prices, compound annual change 2025 to 2035: electricity 13.48 to 16.62 cents per kWh (Table 8, 2.12% a year), natural gas 10.35 to 15.46 dollars per MMBtu (Table 3, 4.09% a year). Discount rate for NPV: PRODUCT DECISION, 8% default for commercial investment analysis (editable), with 3% as an alternative scenario; not an externally validated figure (docs/15).

endUseSource: End-use split and fuel mix: EIA Commercial Buildings Energy Consumption Survey (CBECS) 2018, Table E1 (major fuels by end use) and Table E5 (electricity by end use), Lodging, released December 2022. Lodging uses 598 trillion Btu: space heating 18.1%, cooling 6.9%, ventilation 14.5%, water heating 18.6%, lighting 8.4%, cooking and refrigeration 17.2% (kitchen), office equipment and computing 1.8% (equipment), other 14.5%. Electric share from E5 at 3,412 Btu per kWh: water heating 15%, cooking and refrigeration 40%, other 82%. National figures (CBECS lodging also includes nursing homes); a Chicago hotel likely uses more for heating.

smartControlFan.source: CALIBRATED to the Illinois Statewide TRM v14.0, Vol. 2, measure 4.4.8 Guest Room Energy Management: for a Chicago hotel with central hot-water fan coils and gas heat it deems 92 to 147 kWh and 3.0 to 6.5 therms saved per ton of guest-room cooling a year (with or without housekeeping setback). At 0.75 to 1.0 ton per room (assumption; the TRM gives no default) that is about 6,900 to 14,700 kWh for 100 rooms. The setback alone gives about 4,900 kWh, because the measure also controls the room's fan coil, which the setback model does not. With smart controls, guest-room fan energy during empty hours is cut by this share; 0.06 to 0.28 lands inside the TRM range and 0.17 puts the model near its middle. Modest for a fan switched from always-on to cycling.

heatingSystems.source: PRODUCT DECISION on documented values: heating site energy = the CBECS lodging heating share (treated as a gas-heated hotel at 80% seasonal efficiency) x 0.80 / system efficiency. Gas boiler or rooftop furnace 80% (typical existing stock, GSA evaluation; IL-TRM uses 80% AFUE for gas in its lighting interaction factors); electric resistance 100%; heat pump COP 2.3 (the IL-TRM v14.0 section 4.5 conversion for heat-pump-heated spaces). Cooling efficiency differences between systems are not modeled.

hotWaterSource: Hot water per occupied room (20 gallons a day, default): cross-checked against the IL-TRM v14.0 Vol. 2, measure 4.3.2 table (from the 2007 ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Applications, ch. 49): hotels use 14 gallons of hot water per room per day (motels 20), about 25% from faucets. At 65% occupancy, 20 gallons per occupied room is about 13 per room, consistent.
comfortSource: PRODUCT DECISION: comfort warnings at occupied heating below 67 F or cooling above 77 F, common-area HVAC under 20 hours, vacant setback below 58 F or above 82 F, and vacant limits of 55 F and 85 F. These are team choices for flagging, not values taken from ASHRAE Standard 55 (a paid standard that was not consulted); they should be reviewed against it.
seasonalOccupancySource: PLACEHOLDER shape, synthetic: monthly multipliers on the annual occupancy, peaking in summer. Annual anchor: Chicago central business district occupancy was 69.2% in 2025 and 68.1% in 2024 (STR, Choose Chicago 2025 Hotel Performance report, January 2026); Choose Chicago publishes annual figures only, so the monthly shape is not sourced. The report also notes a record summer 2025, consistent with a summer peak.

peerBenchmarks.label: ENERGY STAR hotel median (U.S.)
peerBenchmarks.source: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, "U.S. Energy Use Intensity by Property Type" (August 2024): Hotel, median site EUI 63.0 kBtu/ft2 (source EUI 146.7). National, all climates.

peerBenchmarks.label: CBECS lodging mean (U.S.)
peerBenchmarks.source: EIA Commercial Buildings Energy Consumption Survey 2018, Table C1: lodging, mean site EUI 85.7 kBtu/ft2. National, all climates; the lodging category includes nursing homes and dormitories.

endUseClimateSource: Chicago (ASHRAE 5A) end-use split: NLR (formerly NREL) ComStock 2025 Release 3 (AMY 2018), OEDI data lake, end-use-load-profiles-for-us-building-stock/2025/comstock_amy2018_release_3 (CC-BY-4.0), timeseries aggregates by ASHRAE IECC climate zone 2006 = 5A, baseline (upgrade 0), large and small hotels combined (667.6 million ft2 represented): heating 21.9% (all fuels), cooling 10.6% (incl. heat rejection), ventilation 6.4% (fans 5.1, pumps 1.2, heat recovery 0.2), lighting 8.9% (interior 7.0, exterior 1.9), hot water 19.1%, kitchen 15.0% (natural gas interior equipment, mainly cooking), electric interior equipment and refrigeration 18.1%, split between 'equipment' and 'other' in the CBECS ratio (1.8 : 14.5). Other climates keep the CBECS 2018 national lodging split (endUseShareOfSite).
euiSource: Site EUI for Chicago 92.3 kBtu/ft2: NLR (formerly NREL) ComStock 2025 Release 3 (AMY 2018), OEDI data lake, end-use-load-profiles-for-us-building-stock/2025/comstock_amy2018_release_3 (CC-BY-4.0), zone 5A hotels (large 93.5, small 84.7; Illinois hotels 93.6 from the by-state annual results). The default 92 for other climates stays a placeholder. Age factor (relative to the Illinois hotel average 93.6, area-weighted, ComStock Illinois annual results, 264 hotel samples): built before 1980 96.9 kBtu/ft2 (x1.035), 1980-1999 88.6 (x0.947), 2000 and later 95.9 (x1.025). Vintage is confounded with HVAC system type (PTAC with electric heat about 77, fan coils with chiller and boiler about 121 kBtu/ft2), so the factor is a stock average, not an effect of age alone. CBECS 2018 Table C1 (all buildings) shows no consistent trend by year constructed (62-80 kBtu/ft2).
